interpretation: If everything moved is moved by something, either by a thing moved by another or not, there must be a mover not moved by another (ἀνάγκη τι εἶναι κινοῦν ὃ οὐχ ὑπʼ ἄλλου πρῶτον). Stated as a reductio, as the prima via's conclusion is. It is weaker than the prima via's 'moved by none': Aristotle goes on (256a19-21) to say that such a first mover, if moved, moves itself; that further step is not formalized here.
